subject: Clarify outbound egress origins and firewall wiring for Private Runtime
content:
From: Samantha Lee <secops@edgehealth.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@edgehealth.com
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private runtime — minimal outbound profile and firewall wiring

Hi Lukas,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. Our security team needs a short, unambiguous list of the outbound IPs/FQDNs and the firewall behaviors required so we can sign off and move forward with procurement. Two quick asks to unblock us: 

1) A minimal set of destination IP ranges (or FQDNs) that must be allowed from our VPC to the Redwood Private runtime/agents.
2) Any expected source IP behavior (ephemeral NAT ranges, port expectations, SNI, TLS fingerprinting) we must express in our firewall and outbound rules.

We have a few procurement constraints: the ops team prefers IPs rather than wide FQDN allowances, and legal wants any SLA/contract language that references network dependencies called out explicitly. We attached our internal template (attached) and will need a short paragraph for the contract describing egress responsibilities.

Can you reply with the minimal allowlist + a recommended contract sentence by EOD?

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Lead SecOps — EdgeHealth

On Mon, Aug 23, 2026 at 09:42 AM, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
To: Samantha Lee <secops@edgehealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private runtime — minimal outbound profile and firewall wiring

Hi Samantha — great to meet yesterday. Below is a concise starting point that matches how our private runtime (VPC connector) behaves. I kept it intentionally minimal so your ops team can implement quickly.

SUMMARY (minimal):
- Destinations: Allow outbound TCP/443 to the following FQDNs (preferred): api.redwood-inference.com, pods-us.redwood-inference.com.
- IPs: If you require IPs, allow the CIDR blocks 34.201.128.0/20 and 54.86.0.0/18 (these are our edge egress ranges for US-hosted private connectors).
- Ports: 443 only (TLS). We do not require other outbound ports for the control plane.
- TLS: Strict TLS 1.2+ with SNI set to the target FQDN. We also support TLS 1.3.
- Fingerprinting: No proprietary TLS fingerprint required; SNI + cert validation is sufficient.
- Ephemeral behavior: Source IPs will NAT to the CIDR ranges above; they are relatively stable but may change with capacity scaling — we provide advance notice for planned range rotations.
- Fallback: In degraded scenarios we may failover to a regional relay (pods-eu.redwood-inference.com) — allow the hostnames rather than pinning to single IPs if you want smoother fallbacks.

CONTRACT LANGUAGE (suggested paragraph):
"EdgeHealth will permit outbound TLS connections from customer-hosted connectors to Redwood Inference control plane endpoints (api.redwood-inference.com and associated regional pods) over TCP/443. Redwood Inference will publish and maintain the set of egress CIDR blocks used for NATing outbound traffic and provide at least 30 days notice prior to planned changes to those CIDRs. Either party may request a technical review if changes materially affect the permitted firewall configuration."

I attached a short matrix (private-deploy-egress-matrix.xlsx) with explicit FQDN-to-IP mappings and a proposed firewall rule set (fw-rules-proposal.pdf).

Next steps: David and Kimberly will add the operational firewall snippets and call out any implications for your procurement/legal ask.

— Lukas

On Mon, Aug 23, 2026 at 10:05 AM, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai> wrote:

Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private runtime — minimal outbound profile and firewall wiring

Adding a few operational clarifications from our networking team: 

- If EdgeHealth requires strict IP-only allowlisting (no FQDNs), use the two CIDR blocks above as the primary set. We will publish any additional ephemeral blocks in the shared Drive folder and tag changes.
- For HTTPS inspection scenarios: our certificate chain uses public CA certs; do not proxied-terminate (MITM) TLS — instead allow passthrough to the hostnames above. If your enterprise policy mandates TLS inspection, we recommend an allowlist exception for the Redwood FQDNs to preserve mTLS/certificate validation.
- Health-checks & keepalives: the runtime occasionally opens short-lived TLS sessions for control-plane telemetry; timeouts should be >= 5s.
- DNS: If you pin by IP, ensure DNS TTLs are respected; we sometimes rotate underlying IPs during scale events.

Operational firewall snippet (example):
- Source: EdgeHealth VPC CIDR (e.g. 10.12.0.0/16)
- Destination: 34.201.128.0/20, 54.86.0.0/18
- Protocol: TCP
- Port: 443
- Application: TLS
- Notes: Permit SNI-based routing to api.redwood-inference.com

I'll follow up with a short page listing how we notify IP range changes and the cadence for those updates.

— David

Hi Samantha — quick contract note from our side to help your legal/procurement teams: 

1) We can accept the suggested contract paragraph Lukas provided, but procurement often asks for an explicit SLA carve-out regarding network-induced outages. Suggested supplement: "Network-related outages (connectivity between EdgeHealth and Redwood endpoints) will be excluded from Redwood's system uptime SLA when caused by the customer’s firewall or network configuration; Redwood will provide diagnostic artifacts and collaboration per the Support SLA to remediate such issues."

2) Lead time for IP changes: we commit to 30 days' notice for planned changes; emergency rotations may be shorter — in those rare cases we will provide automated push notifications and a rollback path.

3) Attachments: Marissa will send a single PDF that shows the exact firewall allowlist snippet we recommend for sign-off (binary-friendly for their ops team).

Kimberly Park
Director, Field Ops Contracts — Redwood Inference
